This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C.

- Section B: answer 2 questions out of 3 and

In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed.

*Section C: answer all questions in this section.*

In order to determine the concentration of a dilute sulphuric acid solution, a student is provided with the following solutions and equipment: 0.25 M NaOH, dilute HCl, pipette, burette, conical flask, phenolphthalein indicator, clamp and stand.

figures.legende: Burette readings (initial and final) for Experiment 1 and Experiment 2.

Points imprimés 3 (a), 3 (b), 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 8 (c), 6 (d) = 20 : cohérents avec « Total = 20 marks » ; ceux de (c) sont regroupés dans la sous-question (c) (8).

Lecture des burettes (c)(i) : les échelles dessinées sont irrégulières ; lecture retenue 0,0 / 16,1 (expérience 1) et 10,1 / 26,2 (expérience 2), soit deux titres de 16,1 cm3 (précision ± 0,1 cm3). Lecture alternative au bas du ménisque : 0,0 / 16,2 et 10,2 / 26,3 (titres 16,2 et 16,1, moyenne 16,15), donnant 0,19 M également. Le résultat final reste 0,19 M.

La liste de matériel imprimée cite « dilute HCl » alors que la question porte sur l'acide sulfurique (« dilute sulphuric acid ») : l'acide sulfurique est retenu (rapport 1 : 2), l'autre lecture est notée dans le corrigé.

questions.enonce_markdown: Draw the experimental set up you would use. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(The learner draws the diagram described below and labels it.)*

- A **retort stand with a clamp** holds a **burette vertically**; the burette contains the **dilute acid** (filled using a small funnel which is then removed), with the tap at the bottom and the meniscus on a graduation.
- Directly below the tap, a **conical flask** stands on a **white tile (or white paper)** so that the colour change is easy to see. It contains **25.0 cm$^3$ of 0.25 M NaOH** and 3 drops of **phenolphthalein** (pink solution).
- Label: burette, clamp and stand, tap, acid, conical flask, NaOH + phenolphthalein, white tile.

During the titration the acid is run from the burette into the flask, swirling the flask all the time, until the end-point is reached.

questions.enonce_markdown:
25 cm$^3$ of 0.25 M NaOH was transferred into a conical flask and 3 drops of phenolphthalein indicator was added.

(i) Sketch and name the apparatus used to transfer the NaOH solution.

(ii) Identify the liquid that is used to rinse the conical flask. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) A **pipette** (a 25 cm$^3$ **volumetric pipette**, used with a pipette filler). *Sketch:* a long thin glass tube with a wide bulb in the middle, a single graduation mark on the upper narrow neck, and a narrow tip at the bottom.

(ii) **Distilled water.** The flask is rinsed only with distilled water, which does not change the number of moles of alkali placed in it. (The burette is rinsed with the acid and the pipette with the alkali, but never the conical flask, because that would add extra reagent.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
The dilute acid was run from the burette and two accurate results were recorded as shown on the following diagrams:

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2019-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_9_fig_1.png)

(i) Read and record the results of experiment 1 and 2 on the following table. *[3 marks]*

| | Experiment 1 | Experiment 2 |
|---|---|---|
| final reading | | |
| initial reading | | |
| Titre | | |

(ii) Determine the mean titre of the dilute sulphuric acid used. *[1 mark]*

(iii) What will be the colour change to indicate the end of the experiment? *[1 mark]*

(iv) Calculate the concentration of the dilute sulphuric acid solution if 25 cm$^3$ of 0.25 M NaOH was required. *[2 marks]*

(v) In carrying out this experiment the acid accidentally spilled on the student's hands. Advise the student on what should be done. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) Readings are taken at the **bottom of the meniscus** to the nearest 0.1 cm$^3$ (the scale is read downwards on a burette):

| | Experiment 1 | Experiment 2 |
|---|---|---|
| final reading (cm$^3$) | 16.1 | 26.2 |
| initial reading (cm$^3$) | 0.0 | 10.1 |
| Titre (cm$^3$) | 16.1 | 16.1 |

Titre = final reading - initial reading: $16.1 - 0.0 = 16.1$ and $26.2 - 10.1 = 16.1$. The two titres agree, so they are accurate results.

(ii) Mean titre $= \dfrac{16.1 + 16.1}{2} = 16.1\ \mathrm{cm^3}$.

(iii) The acid is added to the alkali, so phenolphthalein changes from **pink (in alkali) to colourless (in acid)** at the end-point.

(iv) Equation: $2\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{Na_2SO_4} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$ (1 mol of acid reacts with 2 mol of alkali).

Amount of NaOH: $n = \dfrac{0.25 \times 25}{1000} = 0.00625\ \mathrm{mol}$.

Amount of $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$: $n = \dfrac{0.00625}{2} = 0.003125\ \mathrm{mol}$, contained in $16.1\ \mathrm{cm^3} = 0.0161\ \mathrm{dm^3}$.

Concentration $= \dfrac{0.003125}{0.0161} = 0.194\ \mathrm{mol\,dm^{-3}}$.

**Answer: about 0.19 M** (0.19 mol per dm$^3$).

*(Note: the printed list of equipment mentions dilute HCl, but the question asks about sulphuric acid. If a candidate treated the acid as a monobasic acid, $\mathrm{NaOH} + \mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{H_2O}$, he would get $0.00625 / 0.0161 = 0.39$ M; the sulphuric acid ratio 1 : 2 is the one asked for.)*

(v) Wash the hands **immediately with a large amount of running water** for several minutes to dilute and remove the acid, and report the accident to the teacher or laboratory attendant (seek medical attention if the skin stays red or painful).

questions.enonce_markdown:
You are given the following gases: $\mathrm{H_2}$, $\mathrm{SO_2}$, $\mathrm{NH_3}$.

Sketch the apparatus you would use to collect a pure sample of each gas in the laboratory. *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
*(The learner sketches a labelled diagram for each gas. The method of collection depends on the density and solubility of the gas.)*

**1. Hydrogen, $\mathrm{H_2}$** (made from zinc and dilute hydrochloric acid: $\mathrm{Zn} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow \mathrm{ZnCl_2} + \mathrm{H_2}$). Hydrogen is **almost insoluble in water**, so collect it **over water**: a flask with a thistle funnel and delivery tube leading into a gas jar (or test tube) full of water, inverted in a trough of water. The gas displaces the water downwards. This gives a pure (but wet) sample. (It can also be collected by upward delivery, because it is lighter than air, but over water is purer.)

**2. Sulphur dioxide, $\mathrm{SO_2}$** (for example from sodium sulphite and dilute acid: $\mathrm{Na_2SO_3} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{SO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$). $\mathrm{SO_2}$ is **very soluble in water and denser than air**, so it cannot be collected over water: collect it by **downward delivery (upward displacement of air)**: the delivery tube goes to the bottom of an upright gas jar, with a loose cover; the gas may first be dried by bubbling through concentrated sulphuric acid. It is toxic: work in a fume cupboard.

**3. Ammonia, $\mathrm{NH_3}$** (from ammonium chloride and calcium hydroxide, heated). $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is **very soluble in water and less dense than air**, so it is collected by **upward delivery (downward displacement of air)**: the delivery tube goes to the top of an **inverted gas jar**. The gas is first **dried by passing it through a tower of quicklime (calcium oxide)**. Concentrated sulphuric acid cannot be used as it reacts with ammonia.
